sections.heading: What fertility means
body: Fertility means being able to get pregnant and carry a pregnancy.
Many women and couples take time to get pregnant. This is common.
Around 1 in 6 adults in the world have trouble getting pregnant at some point in their life (World Health Organization, 2023). You are not alone.

sections.heading: When to see a health worker
body: Common advice is to see a health worker if you have been trying to get pregnant for 12 months and you are under 35 years old.
If you are 35 or older, common advice is to go after 6 months of trying.
Go sooner if your periods are very irregular or have stopped, if your periods are very painful, or if you have had infections or surgery in the past.

sections.heading: Possible reasons
body: There are many possible reasons why getting pregnant can take longer. Some are linked to ovulation or hormones, such as PCOS. Others include endometriosis, fibroids, blocked tubes or past infections.
Sometimes the reason is with the man. Sometimes no clear reason is found.
Only a health worker, with tests, can find the reason. This app cannot tell you what is causing it.

sections.heading: Both partners matter
body: Trouble getting pregnant is not only a woman's issue. A man can also be tested, often with a simple semen test.
Nobody should be blamed. Going to the clinic together can help.

sections.heading: What a check-up may involve
body: A health worker may ask about your periods, past pregnancies, your health and how long you have been trying.
They may suggest blood tests, a scan, or a test for your partner. Ask them to explain each test and why you need it.

costs.title: Understand the costs
costs.intro: This app does not show prices yet. We will only show a price when a clinic has confirmed it, with the date it was checked.

sections.heading: Seeing a health worker
body: Seeing a doctor or nurse usually has a fee. Fees are different at public and private clinics.

sections.heading: Tests
body: Blood tests, scans and semen tests may each have their own fee. Ask the clinic what each test costs before you agree to it.

sections.heading: Medicine and treatment
body: If a doctor suggests treatment, ask what it costs, how long it lasts and whether there are cheaper options.

sections.heading: Transport and time
body: Think about bus fare, time off work and how many visits you may need.

sections.heading: Questions to ask about cost
body: How much is the first visit?
What tests might I need, and what do they cost?
Do you accept medical aid?
Can I pay in parts?

urgent.heading: Get help now
body: Go to the nearest clinic or hospital straight away if you have very strong pain in your belly (especially on one side), heavy bleeding, or if you faint or feel like you will faint.

sections.heading: You are not alone
body: Trying to get pregnant can bring stress, sadness or worry. These feelings are normal.
Talking to someone you trust, a counsellor or a support group can help.

sections.heading: Pressure from family
body: Some women face blame or pressure from family. The reason can be with either partner. It is no one's fault.

sections.heading: Next steps
body: Write down your questions. Use the Prepare for care checklist. Look for a clinic in Find care.

sections.heading: What we collect
body: Nothing. You do not need an account, a name or a phone number.

sections.heading: What stays on your phone
body: Your checklist ticks and your questions to the assistant are kept only while the app is open. They are cleared when you close the app. Your language choice is not saved either.

sections.heading: No tracking
body: This app has no analytics, no adverts and no trackers. Your answers are not sent anywhere.

The only exception is Smart answers in Ask. When it is on, your question, your pathway answers and your last few questions are sent to our server to write an answer. Nothing is saved. You can turn it off in Ask.

sections.heading: Sharing and calls
body: If you press Share, your phone opens its own share menu and you choose where the summary goes.
If you press Call, your phone opens its dialler. The call is between you and the clinic.

sections.heading: Report a problem
body: If you see something wrong or unsafe in this app, please tell the Intelligent Fertility Navigator team. Contact details will be added before launch.

see.heading: It is a good time to see a health worker
see.body: Based on your answers, book a visit soon. Use Prepare for care to get ready.

wait.heading: You can keep trying for now
wait.body: Many couples need more time. Come back and check again after 12 months of trying if you are under 35, or after 6 months if you are 35 or older.

steps.text: Having sex every 2 to 3 days through the month gives a good chance without tracking exactly.
Eat well, stay active and stop smoking if you smoke. This helps both partners.
If you may have had an infection, ask a health worker for a test and treatment. Untreated infections can harm fertility.
Ask your partner to be tested too. A simple semen test is part of a fertility check.
